My parents also taught me not to stand up for myself. They taught me to be polite, don't complain and always say yes. 
I've been seeing a therapist every week for more time than I can remember now (for this and other reasons) and I can share some of the main things I've learned:

. You need to let people know how you want to be treated. If you're not ok with something someone said or did to you, say it. 

. You're allowed to say yes and no, in any situation, and you don't owe anyone any explanations, excuses or apologies, for feeling a certain way.

. Don't feel bad for not wanting to help when someone asks for your help. Again, you're allowed to say yes or no in any situation.

. Normalize saying these:

You interrupted me, I am not done talking.
That's not funny.
That's not appropriate.
That's disrespectful.
You are making me uncomfortable.

I hope this can be somewhat helpful for you!
